subject: Science
theme: Indian space program - IRS satellite series development and launch chronology
question_short_text: Which IRS satellite was launched from India in 1996?
text: Which one of the following satellites is to be launched from India in 1996?
explanation: IRS-P3 was successfully launched on March 21, 1996, by ISRO using the PSLV-D3 launch vehicle from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota. It was an experimental remote sensing satellite for Earth observation applications.

research.summary: IRS-P3 was launched on March 21, 1996, marking a critical milestone in India's remote sensing programme. The 'P' in IRS-P3 stands for 'Polar' and the '3' denotes it was the third experimental mission in the IRS-P series. It was carried into orbit by PSLV-D3, which represented the third developmental flight of India's Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle—a significant achievement in itself, as this was only India's second successful PSLV test flight after PSLV-D2. IRS-P3 was lighter (930 kg) than its operational counterparts and served primarily as a technology demonstrator. It carried two remote sensing payloads: the Wide Field Sensor (WiFS), similar to IRS-1C but with an additional Short Wave Infrared band, and the Modular Opto-electronic Scanner (MOS) developed by Germany's DLR in cooperation with ISRO. Uniquely, IRS-P3 also carried an Indian X-ray Astronomy Experiment (IXAE) for astronomical observations and a C-band transponder for radar calibration. Unlike operational satellites of the period, IRS-P3 had no on-board data recorder; all sensor data were transmitted in real-time to ground stations in Hyderabad and Neustrelitz (Germany). The satellite operated for over 9 years and 10 months, exceeding its design life of 3 years. Timing-wise, IRS-P3 came after IRS-P2 (October 1994) and before IRS-1D (September 1997), fitting into a development sequence that validated new technologies for the next-generation IRS-1C and 1D satellites. The question tests aspirants' knowledge of the IRS launch chronology and the distinction between operational (1A, 1B, 1C, 1D) and experimental P-series satellites.
facts: IRS-1A (March 1988) was India's first indigenous remote sensing satellite, launched from Baikonur, USSR, using a Vostok-2M booster. It carried LISS-I and LISS-II cameras and operated for 8 years 4 months.
IRS-1C was launched on December 28, 1995 (before IRS-P3) with improved spatial resolution and PAN, LISS-III, and WiFS payloads. It was the first second-generation operational satellite.

The P-series IRS satellites (P2, P3, P4, P5, P6) were experimental or specialized missions designed to test new technologies or serve specific application areas before being incorporated into operational systems.
PSLV-D3 (March 1996) was the second successful test flight of India's indigenous launch vehicle, a critical validation that enabled the PSLV to become India's primary carrier for polar missions.

IRS satellites are placed in Sun-synchronous polar orbits at approximately 817–820 km altitude with near-polar inclinations, enabling consistent Earth observation for agriculture, forestry, water resources, and disaster management.
